facts.fact: Le Quotidien reports the first phase of the national interoperability platform, UXP, was completed in 2025 in five ministries, with first applications deployed in 2024.
Le Quotidien reports a contract signed with Cybernetica for phase two, running to end-2027, to integrate the platform across all ministries.
Cybernetica states phase 1 introduced UXP to five key ministries and institutions.

Cybernetica states a phase 2 contract was signed with the Ministries of Communication Technologies and of Economy and Planification, extending the platform to RNE, TIA, APII, CEPEX, the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank, scheduled to complete in 2027.
CNI's page describes a national X-Road interoperability platform with three pilot services (tax situation, death notification, payslip), without a date on the page; published date used.

slug: 2024-02-14 National interoperability platform in Tunisia (Cybernetica UXP)

facts.fact: Cybernetica states UXP was deployed as a proof of concept for five ministries, with the governing authority set up and five member organisations onboarded, in the go-live phase of Phase 1.

note: Tej is described as a tax-exchange platform for filing and supplier tax checks; the document does not say it carries data between public bodies' systems, so no exchange fact.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Communication Technologies' workshop statement says the UXP national interconnection platform was presented and the project launched in a first phase with four ministries (Interior, Education, Transport, Social Affairs), to extend to the other ministries in a second phase; the page has no dateline, so the published year is used.

note: The implementing decree sets the operator's tasks, including putting the platform into service, and two committees; it states no platform built, piloted or live.
The decree-law defines the interoperability platform and names the CNI to set up and run it; it does not say a platform is built, piloted or live.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Communication Technologies presented the new national interoperability platform UXP at a workshop on 7 February 2024 and said the project was launched in a first phase with four ministries (Interior, Education, Transport, Social Affairs), to be extended to the other ministries in a second phase; the document does not say data is yet flowing.

note: Procurement notice of 2026-09-03 for consultants to draft a health-sector interoperability framework; a plan with nothing contracted, delivered or adopted, and no statement on this study.

facts.fact: The playbook names the Plateforme Nationale d'Interoperabilite, operated by the Centre National Informatique, carrying exchanges of citizen register data with state structures including civil status, schools, universities, vocational training and health, under decree-law 2020-31 and decree 2020-777.
A chart in the playbook shows exchanges of citizen register data with state structures rising from 476,052 to 900,125,547, the last of seven yearly values plotted for 2019-2025.

The deck lists setting up a national interoperability system on the Estonian X-Road model, and shows a National Interoperability Platform operated by the Centre National Informatique linking sector systems to the IUC.

facts.fact: A March 2024 ministerial council set up a commission to propose, among other things, generalising the national interoperability platform, reported by allAfrica.

note: Data exchange between administrations is a stated priority and a once-only rule; no platform stated in service or under way.

facts.fact: The ministry's 2027 goals, per the parliamentary committee report, include expanding the existing national interoperability platform to all ministries and reaching 200 interoperability services between public structures.
